q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Data check first: the data does not agree with the premise — ROAS did not increase. Over 2026-10-07 → 2026-10-13 net ROAS (order-date) fell (≈0.80x vs 0.88x in the prior week, about -9.9% vs the immediate prior week), while net profit worsened to INR -69,428 for the same week.

What’s behind it
- Net profit fell mainly because P&L ad spend rose sharply: ad spend (P&L basis) moved from a usual ~₹319,165 to ₹375,394 for the week, an adverse effect on net profit of about ₹56,229 (≈94% of the net profit change). This is the dominant driver. 
- Contribution margin slipped slightly: contribution margin moved from ~₹309,733 to ₹305,966 (≈-₹3,767, ≈6% of the net profit change). That added to the profit decline but was small vs ad spend. 
- ROAS did not rise — it fell because ad spend per order increased (~+21%) while contribution margin per order only rose modestly (+9%), leaving overall net ROAS down ~10%. Campaign- and channel-level checks point to paid activity in ig_feed and a Google PMax campaign as the largest contributors to the shift in returns and spend allocation.

Certainty and data notes
- The accounting identity net profit = contribution margin − ad spend (P&L basis) reconciles exactly here, so the numbers above are arithmetic; the diagnosis found no single upstream event (like a bid edit) that conclusively “caused” it. Some tax lines failed to fetch but do not change the headline. 

Period: 2026-10-07..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
